requirement: Render the union of the header, hit windows, and trailer in source order. Copy retained bytes verbatim and replace each nonempty omitted region of the enclosing item with the literal `...`, including a gap at the beginning or end. Insert the marker directly at the cut. When the retained spans cover the item, the excerpt is its original text.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.graph.search.omissions` has no structural obligations, so no implementation roots are needed. Every clause describes observable output only:

- "Render the union of the header, hit windows, and trailer in source order" fixes which spans appear and in what order. A different construction would give the same excerpt, for example sorting and merging spans, marking a byte mask, or building the excerpt in one pass.
- "Copy retained bytes verbatim" fixes the content of the retained spans. It names no function, type or library.
- "replace each nonempty omitted region ... with the literal `...`, including a gap at the beginning or end" and "Insert the marker directly at the cut" fix the output at each gap. The way gaps are detected is open.
- "When the retained spans cover the item, the excerpt is its original text" is another statement about output.

The text names no required library, algorithm, signature, type, field, or delegation through a named interface. Any implementation that gives these results satisfies it. A test can verify this behavior, and the structural-evidence criterion has nothing to check here.

behavioral: The obligations are: (1) render header ∪ hit windows ∪ trailer in source order; (2) copy retained bytes verbatim; (3) replace each nonempty omitted region with `...`, including at the beginning or end, and put the marker directly at the cut; (4) when the retained spans cover the item, return the original text with no marker. The reviewed tests cover each of these.

- **Marker at the end, none at the start, verbatim multibyte text.** `root_hits_clip_context_to_utf8_boundaries` searches `éhit猫` with `window_bytes` 2 and expects `éhit...`. The leading gap is empty, so there is no leading marker. The trailing gap is nonempty, so there is a trailing marker. The retained `é` is copied verbatim. It also checks that the default window returns the whole source with no marker.
- **Markers at both ends.** `default_windows_retain_128_bytes_on_each_side` expects `...aaa…猫hit猫zzz...` with a leading and trailing `...`. With `window_bytes` 1 it expects `...hit...`, where the multibyte characters are clipped away and the marker sits at the cut.
- **Header, trailer and interior gaps in source order.** `separated_hit_windows_preserve_the_function_declaration` expects `fn run() {...    hit(); hit();
...    hit();
...}` for window 4 and `fn run() {...hit...hit...hit...}` for window 0. These show the header, interior gaps with a marker directly at each cut, and a trailer that ends the item with no extra trailing marker. They also show the union in source order and verbatim multiline text.
- **Coverage gives the original text.** `touching_windows_keep_the_contiguous_source` has two windows that touch. The excerpt must equal `item.text()`, so there is no marker at an empty gap. The first test, `search_groups_exact_occurrences_and_records_the_selected_declaration`, has overlapping and covering windows and expects the full item text as the excerpt.

I found no requirement-violating behavior that these assertions would accept. The cases where a window abuts the header or trailer without a gap, and the empty-gap case in general, are exercised by the touching-windows and `éhit...` cases. The tests are marked `{test}` for the subject.
